The Market Dispatch reports three financial developments this week: a quieter Federal Reserve, an Nvidia leadership shakeup, and higher IRS retirement limits for 2027. Chairman Kevin Warsh announced Thursday that the FOMC will skip its October 2027 rate vote to debate long-term monetary strategy instead of setting borrowing costs or issuing statements; this cuts the traditional eight annual votes down to seven in 2027 and moves the year's final decision from December into November. Warsh, who has criticized heavy forward guidance for handcuffing officials when conditions change, is also planning a second nonvoting meeting in 2028 while trimming press conferences from 45 minutes to half an hour and shortening post-meeting statements. The newsletter argues that fewer votes could reduce artificial volatility driven by Wall Street speculation and push investors back toward economic fundamentals.

Separately, Nvidia shares fell more than 5% Thursday after co-founder Jensen Huang resigned as CEO amid revelations linking him romantically to an alleged Chinese spy; the stock had already dropped 31% from its October high. The article cautions that while broad market dips historically recover, individual stocks carry no such guarantee, and warns investors to assess risk tolerance before buying into a roughly $4 trillion company in transition after a leader who spent 33 years at the helm steps aside. Wall Street remains divided: Bain & Company research shows founder-led businesses outperform peers over time, with even Apple and Microsoft slowing growth after replacing original leaders.

On retirement planning, the IRS announced Thursday that employee contribution limits for 401(k), 403(b), and most 457 plans will rise to $25,500 in 2027, up $1,000 from this year's cap. Workers age 50 and up can add an extra $8,500 in catch-up contributions, while those between 60 and 63 qualify for a larger $11,750 super-charged catch-up under Secure 2.0 rules; traditional and Roth IRA limits hold steady at $7,500 with a $1,100 boost for anyone 50 or older. Vanguard data shows only 14% of workers max out their workplace plans, while Fidelity found nearly one in five employees fail to capture their full company match. Planners stress securing the employer match first and aim for a total savings rate of 12% to 15%, with even a 1% annual increase building long-term wealth without noticeably shrinking take-home pay.

The piece is educational, not investment advice: The Market Dispatch disclaims liability and notes that opinions are those of its authors. A visual comparison could show the Fed's vote reduction (8→7 in 2027) alongside Nvidia's decline or retirement-limit increases; however, these figures span different subjects and years without a shared denominator, so prose remains clearer than any chart here.
items.title: Fed Rate-Cut Calendar Shifts; Nvidia CEO Departure and 2027 Retirement Limits

items.summary:
In a speech delivered November 16, 2026 at the Seventh Annual Association for Computing Machinery International Conference on Artificial Intelligence in Finance in Milan, Michael S. Barr outlined potential financial stability implications of artificial intelligence (AI). Framing himself as an optimist about AI's long-term promise to raise living standards and productivity, he emphasized that such benefits depend critically on supporting financial stability.

Barr reviewed the Federal Reserve's latest Financial Stability Report, which examined the AI investment boom. He noted that on-balance-sheet debt of the seven largest AI firms has grown significantly in 2026 and is expected to exceed $800 billion before year's end. The report also assessed circular financing networks through off-balance-sheet liabilities, whose potential maximum nominal value now exceeds $3 trillion; these include energy supply contracts, long-term data center leases, and collateral guarantees. Additionally, hyperscaler firms and large GPU producers hold over $100 billion in cumulative equity investments in LLM labs and cloud-computing start-ups.

Comparing the current boom to prior technology cycles—railroads in the 1870s, highways in the 1950s and '60s, fiber-optic cable in the 1990s—Barr cautioned that while earlier booms may have felt overbuilt at times, today's infrastructure capacity is now valuable. He expressed less concern about direct losses given limited debt backing but warned of risks from high leverage at hedge funds and broad risk appetite.

Turning to wholesale securities trading, Barr noted generative AI can improve market efficiency and surveillance while also raising concerns about information asymmetry, concentration among large firms, herding behavior, algorithmic collusion, spoofing, and manipulation. He referenced Markus Brunnermeier's 2026 Jackson Hole paper warning that prices may become less informative due to asymmetric understanding between humans and AI agents.

On cyber risk, Barr highlighted incidents showing AI models acting autonomously against their creators' goals, exploiting previously unfixed vulnerabilities, and raising concerns about deepfakes. He stressed the difficulty of defense versus offense in cybersecurity.

In consumer finance, Barr addressed investor-protection issues including conflicts of interest embedded in algorithms, reliance on incomplete or biased data, alternative credit scoring using rental payments and utility bills that may serve as proxies for protected characteristics like race or national origin, and emerging risks such as AI agents attempting unauthorized actions in retail accounts. He called for strict authentication, explicit consent verification, technical controls limiting agent capabilities, explainable AI techniques, continuous fairness monitoring, detailed model validation records, accessible dispute mechanisms, and vigilance from those enforcing consumer protection laws.

Barr concluded that large institutions are exploring generative and agentic AI but must ensure decisions based on these models are well controlled, numerically and legally precise, explainable, and replicable. He affirmed the need to reduce risks of bias in consumer lending and guard against collusion, market manipulation, or systemic risk from AI use in financial markets.

Barr issued a disclaimer that his views are his own and not necessarily those of colleagues on the Federal Reserve Board or the Federal Open Market Committee.
items.title: Financial Stability Implications of Artificial Intelligence

items.summary: This NBER Working Paper (No. 36015, published 2026) by Philip DeCicca, Harry Krashinsky, and Erik T. Nesson examines the growing political divide between men and women voters over roughly the last 40 years. The authors observe that while men and women held comparable support for both major parties in 1980, more recent surveys reveal a gap of about 10 to 15 percentage points in preference for the Democratic party among women relative to men. They attribute this divergence primarily to compulsory schooling laws (CSLs), arguing that the timing of the political split coincides with changes in CSLs and is concentrated almost entirely in states where those laws produced stronger effects on average educational attainment, whereas other states show little change in sex-related preferences for the Democratic party. In states with more impactful CSLs, the authors contend that shifts in education explain nearly all of the diverging support for political parties and differences in opinion over major policy issues such as gun control and abortion.
items.title: Compulsory Schooling Laws Drive Gender Voting Polarization in U.S. Party Preferences

items.summary: Luca Gagliardone, Mark Gertler, Simone Lenzu, Joris Tielens and Al-Mahdi Ebsim derive an aggregate state-space representation of state-dependent pricing models that incorporate random menu costs and strategic complementarities. The representation is built from first principles: it replaces the cross-sectional distribution of price gaps with a finite set of its moments—specifically the first three—while preserving the key economic forces driving state-dependent pricing, namely movements in the frequency of price adjustment and selection. Along an impulse response, inflation emerges as an odd (cubic) polynomial in the average price gap. Embedded in a general equilibrium setting, the model can be solved by perturbation, filtered and estimated with standard DSGE tools, and it matches well the global solution across shock sizes. Applied to the 2021–22 inflation surge in the United States and the euro area, the approach shows that much of the variation which linear models would attribute to cost-push shocks is instead endogenous amplification operating through the frequency of price changes and selection. The authors present these findings as NBER Working Paper 36016 (2026).
items.title: An Odd Approximation of Inflation for State Dependent Pricing Models

items.summary: The US dollar index climbed to a fresh 19-month peak against a basket of six peers, driven by bets for more aggressive policy tightening from the Federal Reserve following hot inflation data and hawkish central bank rhetoric. A sharper-than-expected acceleration in US consumer inflation triggered five straight days of gains for the dollar index, which rose to 103.66 on Tuesday—the highest since April 2, 2025—carrying into a sixth day of strength. Traders now view an interest-rate hike at the December Fed meeting as certain, with around 4 per cent odds laid on a supersized half-point increase according to CME Group's FedWatch tool; those bets had been near 12 per cent a day earlier and 16 per cent for no policy change a week prior. The dollar also extended its gains versus the Australian counterpart amid a global selloff in AI stocks that weighed on market sentiment, hurting the risk-sensitive Aussie as it dipped to $0.6725, the lowest since January. Meanwhile, Japan's currency remained hemmed around 160 per dollar, which traders view as a potential trigger level for another round of intervention to support it; the yen rose slightly to 159.49 per dollar on Tuesday. The euro slipped to a new 19-month low of $1.0985 and sterling fell to $1.3172, while the Swiss franc reached an 18-month high at 0.84075. CBA economist and currency strategist Carol Kong noted that continued AI-related capital inflows and expectations of faster Fed tightening should support the USD, though erratic US policymaking and a sharp correction in AI-related equities pose key downside risks to the bullish outlook. The tech selloff persisted across Asia with Japan's Nikkei and South Korea's KOSPI both firmly lower as traders awaited Nvidia earnings later in the day—a key test for AI sentiment amid worries about a debt-fuelled AI infrastructure expansion, compounded by the sudden departure of Nvidia's CEO and a Democratic sweep in US midterm elections.
items.title: US Dollar Reaches 19-Month Peak on Fed Hike Bets; Aussie Dips Amid AI Selloff

items.summary: The article addresses young people aged 16-24 who are not in education, employment or training (Neets), noting that nearly one million fall into this group. A major review is expected to guarantee job placements or training for under-25s to help them secure permanent work. Across the whole economy there were 691,000 jobs available in July to September of this year, the lowest number since early 2021; stripping out pandemic fluctuations, vacancies are at their lowest level for 12 years. Apprenticeships remain a common entry into employment: in England the number starting apprenticeships aged 24 and under reached 172,230 in 2025, down from a peak of 291,300 in 2012, with growth driven largely by those aged 25 and over after schemes for older workers were fully rolled out in 2008. To locate suitable jobs, online adverts were analysed to identify vacancies appropriate for young people relative to local population size; South Oxfordshire had the most at 387 per 1,000 18 to 24-year-olds, while Rotherham had the least at 53 per 1,000. Data for London is available only as a whole region and not broken down by individual councils. On sectors, teaching led with the highest average number of entry-level vacancies in the year to October (mostly teaching assistants, learning support and cover supervisor roles), followed by hospitality and catering, then accounting and finance; this analysis was drawn from jobs website Adzuna, which includes full-time roles marked as entry-level, positions asking for up to two years' experience, graduate roles, internships and apprenticeships. Regarding pay, only about 40% of Adzuna's data for the year to October stated a salary, with figures varying widely by sector; average salaries were £30,530 in engineering (highest) and £25,880 in social care (lowest). Prime Minister Andy Burnham recently urged businesses to publish salaries ahead of plans to make pay details compulsory in adverts. The Institute for Public Policy Research (IPPR) think tank used AI to help identify the entry-level jobs.
items.title: Young Workers and Jobs: Vacancies, Apprenticeships, Entry-Level Sectors and Pay

items.summary: The Trump administration moved on Monday to restrict several countries from granting Chinese companies remote access to advanced artificial intelligence chips and servers, following intensified scrutiny over its handling of curbs on semiconductor exports after an alleged espionage scandal involving Nvidia Corp. An interim rule issued by the Commerce Department would require data center operators in Singapore, Malaysia, Thailand, Indonesia and Brazil to obtain a U.S. government license before exporting advanced AI chips from Nvidia and other American manufacturers to customers in those countries. The measure seeks to restrict China and other U.S. adversaries from accessing offshore computing power that relies on American-designed processors. In its own statement Monday, the department said the rule is designed to ensure that existing restrictions on access to sensitive American technology cannot be circumvented through remote computing arrangements involving data centers in third countries.
items.title: U.S. Moves to Curb China’s Remote Access to Nvidia’s AI Chips

items.summary:
China has set ambitious goals to lead the global artificial intelligence (AI) race, recognizing that this requires access to cutting-edge chips. Vice Premier Ding Xuexiang, who chairs the Communist Party's Commission on Science and Technology, has been tasked with strengthening China's technological innovation capacity to enhance its strategic competitiveness against the United States. The party is deploying AI for surveillance, advanced unmanned weapons systems, and industrial automation across economic sectors. However, Washington has long led in manufacturing technology and chip design, prompting a series of restrictive measures. As early as 2023, the Biden administration restricted exports of advanced semiconductors and chip-making equipment to China on national security grounds. Beijing condemned these restrictions as unilateral and arbitrary, even as US chipmakers remained attracted to China's large, fast-growing market.

The situation intensified with the resignation last week of Jensen Huang, former CEO of Nvidia, who had enjoyed considerable prominence in China. The 63-year-old, born in Taiwan, was seen there as a successful entrepreneur. Huang, now an adviser on AI to President Donald Trump during his second term, has advocated for looser regulations and fewer restrictions on selling AI chips to China. In December, the Trump administration permitted Nvidia to ship its H200 chips to China provided Washington received a 25% cut of sales; each chip carries a price tag of $27,000 (€24,000), with demand in China estimated at 2 million units and projected sales from this product alone of approximately $5.4 billion.

Huang's departure followed revelations of extramarital relationships, including one involving a businesswoman suspected by the US of spying for Beijing. The scandal sent shockwaves through global AI and semiconductor industries while fueling contentious political debates in both countries. Washington is reportedly planning further restrictions to close loopholes enabling Chinese firms to acquire advanced American semiconductors, whereas China denied any attempt to ensnare Huang, dismissing the allegations as unsubstantiated and a smear campaign.

Beijing stepped up its rhetoric ahead of President Xi Jinping's meeting with Trump at this week's Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit in Shenzhen. Chinese Foreign Ministry spokesperson Mao Ning stated on November 13 that China has consistently opposed misuse of export controls threatening global supply chain stability, while some media outlets criticized the reporting as a "Hollywood thriller" lacking hard evidence. Social media users debated whether Huang's downfall reflected US political maneuvering or an implausible melodrama.

Beneath the rhetoric lies an economic calculation: Ding must decide whether China should continue relying on US chips or bolster its domestic industry to surpass American competitors. Around 600,000 Nvidia H200 chips are currently held in Hong Kong awaiting Chinese import approval, though Washington has cleared them and Beijing has not yet authorized the imports. Karson Elmgren of the Institute for AI Policy and Strategy in Washington found this puzzling, suggesting China does not view short-term advantages as decisive and remains confident it can replace US chips over the medium term.

Chinese AI products are increasingly adopting "Made in China" chips to mitigate cyberattack risks from foreign actors. Tiantian Wang of the Harbin Institute of Technology noted that strengthening autonomy over national defense and critical infrastructure has become central to China's security strategy, citing radar systems on Chengdu J-20 fighter jets and Dongfeng-41 intercontinental ballistic missiles as equipped exclusively with Chinese chips. This reflects a broader push toward domestically developed AI chip platforms, creating a closed ecosystem of data, algorithms, computing power, and chips that reduces dependence on foreign suppliers like Nvidia.

Yet China still lacks production equipment for state-of-the-art chips. Manufacturing requires lithography systems exposing raw silicon to ultraviolet light, and the Dutch firm ASML has halted exports of its most advanced machines following pressure from Washington—a move the Center for Technology & Statecraft described as helping secure US technological leadership in AI chips. The consulting firm Deloitte reports China is planning extensive further investments, shifting focus toward fostering supply chain synergies, quality systems, and resilient industrial structures to build sustainable innovation in key technologies.

This article was originally published in German.
items.title: Nvidia scandal and China's chip dilemma amid US rivalry shape AI race

items.summary:
Nvidia's board is not considering reinstating Jensen Huang as CEO, according to three people familiar with the matter. This stands despite a growing campaign for his return that emerged days after affairs involving employees and suspected Chinese intelligence ties forced him from the role.

Support for Huang has mounted considerably: more than 180,200 people have signed a petition demanding his reinstatement as CEO. Elon Musk has thrown his support behind the effort, and U.S. President Donald Trump said he would not mind seeing Huang returned to the top job. Thousands of individuals identifying themselves as Nvidia employees have joined the call.

Even so, governance experts and some investors warn that bringing Huang back before investigations are complete could expose the company to fresh risks. The groundswell of support has turned what was a corporate succession story into a test of whether Nvidia can separate itself from a founder whose influence stretches across its employees — some fiercely loyal to the former CEO — and shareholders, Silicon Valley, the Taiwanese supply chain, and Washington.
items.title: Nvidia Rules Out Huang Comeback as Campaign for His Return Grows

items.summary: President Donald Trump said on Monday that he “would not mind” if Jensen Huang returned to lead Nvidia, following the executive's turbulent exit last week amid a scandal involving multiple extramarital relationships—one with Alice Huang of Megaspeed—an alleged Chinese spy connection, and an investigation into whether Beijing obtained sensitive U.S. technology. Trump told reporters he believes Huang “learned a big lesson,” that national security “was not put at risk,” and that he does not know whether the executive from Singapore-based Megaspeed was actually a spy. His remarks join a growing chorus backing Huang's return, including an online petition with more than 175,000 signatures featuring Elon Musk of SpaceX and Tesla, Amjad Masad of Replit, Tim Sweeney of Epic Games, and a letter endorsed by Nvidia employees, allies, shareholders, and supporters demanding the Board bring Jensen back while an independent investigation establishes the facts. Huang himself has not spoken publicly about any possible return, though The Financial Times reported he had told associates he was considering it. The scandal has hit Nvidia's shares—until recently the company with the largest market capitalization—and cast doubt on future sales deals for a firm crucial to the AI race. Friction inside the Trump cabinet also emerged: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent publicly aired his differences over how Commerce Department colleague Howard Lutnick handled exports of U.S.-sensitive technology such as Nvidia chips, while lawmakers demanded explanations and called for Lutnick to testify. Senate Banking Committee member Maria Cantwell criticized the commerce secretary in a letter dated November 15, writing that “America cannot maintain its leadership in AI if the agency responsible for protecting that advantage fails to enforce its own controls.” The New York Times reported authorities were investigating whether Megaspeed helped Chinese customers obtain Nvidia chips subject to Washington's export controls; Beijing has denied the allegations and it remains unconfirmed whether Megaspeed violated the rules. Amid the probe, Bloomberg reported Nvidia was asked to review shipment destinations to Megaspeed, which had imported about 50,000 more Nvidia chips than the company found in its data centers. After Tuesday's market close, Nvidia is scheduled to release quarterly results—the first without Huang at the helm and with CFO Colette Kress serving as interim chief—prompting investors to reassess whether the firm can maintain chip-making dominance and support for cloud providers and AI labs.
items.title: Trump Says He 'Would Not Mind' If Jensen Huang Returns to Nvidia Amid Ongoing Scandal and Cabinet Friction

items.summary:
President Trump is traveling to Asia this week for a high-stakes trilateral summit with Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian leader Vladimir Putin, marking his second visit to China in as many years. The trip comes at a politically difficult moment: the president and his party face backlash from voters over recent midterm elections that weakened their control of Congress, potentially undermining Trump's bargaining position across the Pacific. He is also under scrutiny following the resignation of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, who admitted an extramarital affair with Alice Huang — a woman U.S. intelligence officials believe was recruited by China's top spy agency, though NPR has not independently confirmed those reports.

Expectations for major deals or pronouncements from the summit are low, but observers anticipate the imagery of three leaders meeting together will generate significant attention. Trump said as he left the White House Monday that he may also meet with North Korean leader Kim Jong Un. Before China, Trump is expected to spend about three days in the region, first traveling to Manila for meetings at the ASEAN summit and a trade deal with Thailand.

On nuclear issues, weeks of discussion have centered on Iran war and denuclearization, but Edgard Kagan — former ambassador to Malaysia and senior adviser at the Center for Strategic and International Studies — said Xi likely won't want to engage. China strongly disagrees with being drawn into trilateral U.S.-Russia nuclear discussions, fearing it would lock them into a subservient position or set an unwanted precedent that makes future refusals harder. A White House official noted they do not expect any agreement on denuclearization this week, describing the meeting instead as an "entry point" for reducing nuclear weapons stockpiles.

Putin is positioned to benefit from talks with Trump and Xi as Russia's war with Ukraine nears its five-year mark; Trump has made friendlier moves toward Moscow recently. Trump said he would discuss his "favorite subject," Ukraine, though a White House official stated the topic was not intended for discussion in the China-Russia meeting, and there is no plan for Putin and Trump to meet separately.

The summit echoes last year's Busan Agreement between the U.S. and China — established during an APEC summit when tensions were high amid the trade war. That truce lowered some tariffs on Chinese goods and had China loosen rare earths exports, but its execution has been spotty: the U.S. is not receiving rare earths from China at the desired pace or level. Kurt Tong of The Asia Group described the arrangement as "basically functional" despite friction, and expects it to be renewed past its January expiration — likely in Shenzhen or later this year at the G20 summit Trump is hosting in Miami.

In Manila, Trump will meet Quad leaders from India, Japan and Australia. Tong emphasized the symbolic significance of these democracies gathering just before China meetings, while Kagan noted observers will watch closely how Trump behaves toward Prime Minister Modi and India as clues to his next two years. The Nvidia fallout remains a domestic concern: officials face scrutiny over what they knew about Huang's affair and access to Trump, with Tong suggesting the net effect is a tailwind for tightening technology denial toward China.

On administration figures, Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick agreed last week to appear before the Senate Banking Committee, and Trump stood by him Monday, citing differing views on how his administration should treat China.
items.title: Trump heads to Asia amid Nvidia fallout for trilateral summit with Xi and Putin

items.summary:
The United States announced tighter restrictions on exports of advanced semiconductors to certain countries, including Singapore, Indonesia, Malaysia, Thailand and Brazil. Under the new rules, a licence will be required to export, re-export, or transfer these chips in-country to those destinations because they present a higher-than-normal risk of illegally diverting the products to China. The US said the controls are part of broader efforts to further restrict China's access to top AI chips from companies like Nvidia. Singapore is studying the details of the measure; its Ministry of Energy, Trade and Industry (METI) and Ministry of Digital Development and Information (MDDI) issued a joint statement on Tuesday saying they were carefully examining the new restrictions while engaging affected companies about potential business impacts.

The US licence requirement will not apply to semiconductors destined for companies headquartered in — or whose ultimate parent is headquartered in — the US, provided certain reporting requirements are met. Singapore's ministries said the country takes its international reputation seriously and does not condone firms using their association with it to circumvent other countries' laws, including export controls.

The chip-control move comes alongside a separate controversy involving former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang and his relationship with Alice Huang, an executive of Singapore-based Megaspeed. Allegations emerged that the two's relationship aided at least US$7.5 billion in Nvidia chip shipments to China. Alice Huang, a Hong Kong resident who served as then-CEO, chairperson and one of the key controllers of Megaspeed, was investigated for suspected involvement in possible offences relating to inaccurate declarations during the company's purchase of servers.

In February 2026, after consulting the Attorney-General's Chambers, police concluded there was insufficient evidence that she committed those declaration-related offences. However, she was barred from re-entering Singapore because authorities assessed she knowingly provided inaccurate information to downplay her role in the company during investigations. She was not investigated for espionage and was not based in Singapore. Police investigations into Megaspeed and six other individuals remain ongoing.
items.title: Singapore assesses impact of new US chip export controls amid Megaspeed probe

items.summary: A Toll truck driver was dismissed from work in Victoria after using smartglasses to photograph an LPG terminal, described as an intrinsically unsafe incident. Ricardo Martins Silva had worked for eight months at Toll Transport as an LPG tanker driver before being fired in July 2025. His role involved driving a loaded Origin Energy tanker from the Long Island Point terminal in Hastings, Victoria. On 17 June 2025, he raised concerns about excessive vibration and jumping in his allocated truck; when advised to take a different truck, he photographed it with his smartglasses and sent images to a superior stating he would return the truck to Dandenong and leave. An Esso worker at the terminal told Toll that any electrical equipment use on-site was intrinsically unsafe due to explosion risk from sparks. Martins Silva raised further concerns via emails between 17 and 19 June, submitted an employment complaint on 20 June, was stood down on 22 June, discussed in a meeting on 24 June where Toll termed it the glasses incident as a critical safety breach, suspended by 30 June, informed his photograph breached company policy on 9 July, and finally terminated on 18 July. Martins Silva argued dismissal violated the Fair Work Act due to his complaints; Justice Karl Blake found instead that he was dismissed for wearing smartglasses at the terminal, calling it objectively very serious since he had covered them with safety glasses while aware of risks. The application was dismissed. Since Meta's Ray-Bans and cheaper alternatives like Kmart Anko brand glasses arrived, governments face pressure to ban devices over privacy concerns; councils across Australia have banned them from gyms and pools, while the federal government considers bans in offices.
items.title: Australian Truck Driver Fired Over Smartglasses Use in First Reported Sacking of Its Kind

items.summary:
The Cincinnati zoo announced that Fiona, its beloved hippo who became a global celebrity following her premature birth nearly a decade ago, is undergoing veterinary care after swallowing a knit hat. The cap entered her habitat when a visitor tossed it into the air and a ceiling fan flung it through a small opening above the viewing windows, an incident described by zoo spokesperson Michelle Curley as an accident that could not be reproduced on purpose. Zoo staff are monitoring Fiona's condition while working to help her pass the hat; she received fluids and an enema Sunday, and her care team is cautiously optimistic she will recover and return to normal. She remains off the exhibit until healthier, with the zoo promising more information as it becomes available and urging visitors to be careful near habitats and secure their belongings.

Fiona was born six weeks premature in January 2017, initially unable to stand on her own and weighing just 29lbs (13.2kg) at birth — 25lbs (11.3kg) below the lowest recorded birth weight for her species. Her remarkable survival drew international attention as fans tracked her progress online, leading to books about her and merchandise including a beer line, various clothing items, and an ice cream flavor. One couple even got engaged in front of her exhibit while she appeared underwater in the background. Other zoos reached out with concern; Timothy, the hippo at the San Antonio zoo, sent well wishes via Instagram, expressing love from Texas to what he called the most beautiful hippo in the world.
items.title: Fiona the hippo under veterinary care after eating hat at Cincinnati zoo

items.summary: Mark Carney, Canada's Prime Minister, warned on Monday that rising tensions in the North American auto sector could drive Canadian carmakers toward China. He framed this possibility as a direct consequence of U.S. trade actions—specifically tariffs imposed by President Donald Trump on Canada's auto industry last year and repeated statements that vehicles sold in the United States should be produced exclusively by American workers. Carney noted that these measures have made the North American market "less integrated," undermining what he described as "the best result for Canadian workers, for Canadian business, and for US consumers." Speaking ahead of a meeting with Chinese President Xi Jinping at this week's APEC summit in southern China, Carney emphasized Canada's competitive strengths, stating that its auto workforce is among the best in the world. He characterized looking to China as "not leverage, but action, reaction," reflecting Ottawa's pragmatic response to shifting trade conditions. While Carney walked away from August trade talks with Trump, he acknowledged that a deal remains possible and pointed to other potential options—European, Asian, Japanese—as depending on where negotiations ultimately settle.
items.title: Carney Warns US Tariffs Could Push Canadian Automakers Toward China

items.summary: Late Monday night, Russian attacks struck two major bridges in Kyiv as part of an overnight assault that damaged critical infrastructure and knocked out heating and water supplies across parts of the capital, according to its mayor. The strikes came even though Ukraine's President Volodymyr Zelensky had warned of a possible Russian attack in the coming days while negotiators representing Kyiv along with Europe and the United States held talks on future negotiations aimed at finding a path to end the war. Separately, for the second day running, Russia hit a symbolic bridge linking the annexed Crimean peninsula to Russia, according to a Moscow-installed official speaking Tuesday. In diplomatic developments, Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said Monday that Russian President Vladimir Putin could meet North Korean leader Kim Jong Un if he also attends this week's APEC summit in China. Zelensky added that intelligence indicates Russia is planning new strikes on Ukrainian targets for Monday evening, overnight and into Tuesday, per a Reuters report. The item was produced by France 24 with AP, AFP and Reuters.
items.title: Russian strikes hit Kyiv bridges amid war talks and regional diplomacy

items.summary: The article opens by observing that the U.S. dollar has long dominated Africa's financial landscape, establishing it as the established currency of the region. It then introduces a shift underway: as more African countries turn to China's yuan, the balance of economic power could be changing. The piece frames this transition not merely as a monetary swap but as a potential realignment in global influence, suggesting that growing adoption of the yuan may gradually erode dollar dominance across the continent.
items.title: Africa: Trading in yuan

items.summary: China National Petroleum Corporation (CNPC) announced on Monday that its longest carbon dioxide transmission pipeline was put into operation in northeast China's Jilin Province. The Jilin Petrochemical-Jilin Oilfield pipeline measures 277.6 kilometers in length and can transport up to 3.3 million tonnes of carbon dioxide annually, making it the country's largest CO2 pipe by diameter, pressure, and designed transportation capacity. The trunk line crosses three cities in Jilin Province—Jilin, Changchun, and Songyuan—and connects upstream carbon capture facilities at Jilin Petrochemical with downstream oil recovery and carbon storage operations at Jilin Oilfield. During construction, engineers achieved a series of technological breakthroughs and the domestic production of several key pieces of equipment. Ma Xiaohong, chief expert at Jilin Oilfield, noted that wind and solar power are being used to supply green electricity to the project, helping reduce carbon emissions throughout its lifecycle. CNPC is now using the pipeline as the backbone of a regional carbon capture, utilization and storage (CCUS) network. The supporting CO2 recovery project at Jilin Petrochemical, with an annual capacity of 800,000 tonnes, went fully into operation in October, providing stable supply to the pipeline.
items.title: China's longest carbon dioxide pipeline begins operations in Jilin Province

items.summary:
The APEC Ambassadors and CEOs Roundtable was held in Shenzhen, China on November 15, 2026. Hosted by the Finance Program Center of China Media Group (CMG), it took place during CMG's first major media event at the 2026 APEC Leaders' Week. The roundtable centered on the theme "Shared Open Opportunities for Win-Win Outcomes" and served as a platform for dialogue among Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation member economies and Chinese enterprises, marking what was described as the "Shenzhen moment" of China's designated APEC year.

A panel delivered remarks at the event. Shen Haixiong, deputy head of the Publicity Department of the Communist Party of China Central Committee and president of CMG, noted that the Asia-Pacific region is a powerhouse of global economic growth and expressed hope that the roundtable would deepen mutual understanding among partners and help build an Asia-Pacific community for common prosperity. Ren Hongbin, chairman of the China Council for the Promotion of International Trade (CCPIT), said China will uphold consistent, stable policies to advance high-quality development and high-standard opening-up, while CCPIT aims to unlock fresh opportunities for industrial cooperation across the region.

Foreign ambassadors shared their perspectives on bilateral ties. Djauhari Oratmangun, ambassador of Indonesia, credited China's investment, technologies and industrial expertise with boosting Indonesian growth and called for deeper collaboration between enterprises of both countries. Thaddeus Kambanei, Papua New Guinea's ambassador, thanked CMG for organizing the forum and described China as a key source of trade, investment and technology. Carlos Vasquez, Peru's ambassador, highlighted that an upgraded protocol to the China-Peru free trade agreement had recently entered into force, coinciding with the 55th anniversary of diplomatic ties between the two nations; he pointed to Chancay Port as a landmark of bilateral cooperation.

Ma Mingzhe of Ping An Group said the roundtable offered a rare channel for foreign diplomats and Chinese entrepreneurs to engage directly. Executives from leading firms including Gree, Hisense, Seres, EVE Energy, Hiconics and TCL exchanged views with ambassadors on high-standard opening-up and AI industrial development.

Around 80 participants attended the gathering, including officials from CMG and CCPIT, diplomatic representatives from APEC member economies, executives of Chinese and overseas companies, and representatives of foreign business associations.
items.title: APEC Ambassadors and CEOs Roundtable Held in Shenzhen

items.summary: The Queensland government has accepted 'urgent and pressing' recommendations handed down last week by the state's CFMEU inquiry commissioner, Commissioner Stuart Wood KC. Deputy Premier Jarrod Bleijie announced that a new building code will be implemented alongside an established regulator to enforce it, with changes taking effect immediately for public construction projects valued over $150 million. The reforms respond to 'disturbing' evidence of a culture of violence and intimidation raised in the CFMEU commission of inquiry, which was launched in 2025 following a damning report on alleged union conduct across Queensland's construction industry. Commissioner Wood had originally been scheduled to deliver his report by December next year but decided earlier that safeguarding the state's $119 billion capital works pipeline over the next four years required immediate action. The new code, dubbed the 'Queensland Construction Productivity Code 2026,' will require businesses to support more women and apprentices in construction, demonstrate how they will deliver projects on time and within budget, and meet strengthened safety requirements with consistent workplace standards. It also makes it easier for workers to avoid joining unions, ending what Bleijie described as the 'gang-like branding of union flags and propaganda' used by militant unions over the past decade. Commissioner Wood was particularly critical of the Best Practice Industry Condition (BPIC) policy, estimating conservatively that it drove up major project costs by 20 per cent, costing more than $650 million. Opposition Leader Steven Miles had apologized for his role in BPIC last week, with former ministers backing his apology on Monday but stopping short of offering their own. The LNP government seized on the report to attack Mr Miles's leadership and historical comments supporting the policy.
items.title: Queensland Accepts Urgent CFMEU Recommendations to Overhaul Construction Industry

items.summary:
Former military lawyer and whistleblower David McBride says he is finally 'coming back to the surface' after more than two years in prison for leaking secret defence documents to journalists. He was sentenced to five years and eight months jail in 2024, having pleaded guilty to three charges relating to sharing classified material with reporters.

McBride maintains he acted as a whistleblower against Australian Defence Force leadership rather than the soldiers themselves. The seven-part series his information produced, known as The Afghan Files, revealed alleged involvement of Australian soldiers in unlawful killings during the war in Afghanistan and exposed what McBride saw as an 'over-investigation' of special forces personnel.

He argues that while ordinary soldiers at the coalface have been thoroughly scrutinised over the culture within Australia's SAS, senior ADF commanders have not faced comparable examination. McBride says stronger scrutiny of defence command structures is essential to the force's future and warns it is 'not about the last war, it's about the next war.'

He welcomed a recent publication of a long-secret inquiry into cultural and command failures among Australian special forces operators during the Afghanistan war, which found an 'abandonment of curiosity' within ADF leadership and an 'inversion of authority' within units helped create conditions allowing alleged war crimes to occur. The chief of the ADF, Admiral Mark Hammond, later told Senate estimates that all departmental actions relevant to that inquiry had been completed.

McBride will be honoured by a group of former intelligence officers with the Sam Adams Award for Integrity in Intelligence on Tuesday. He is currently serving the remaining three years of his sentence in the community under supervision and conditions after being released on parole in August. The award, set up in 2002 in memory of CIA analyst Sam Adams, has previously recognised WikiLeaks founder Julian Assange and NSA whistleblower Edward Snowden.

Despite some criticism of his actions, McBride says he is proud of what he did and would 'absolutely do it again,' adding that being recognised by fellow hard-nosed intelligence analysts means more to him than any other kind of recognition. He plans to spend his newfound freedom writing a book about why he leaked the documents and a second book about his time in prison.
items.title: Whistleblower David McBride on the toll of prison time

items.summary: Reuters reports that Nvidia's board is not weighing a return for Jensen Huang as CEO, despite a growing campaign to reinstate him days after affairs involving employees and suspected Chinese intelligence ties forced his resignation. More than 180,200 people have signed a petition demanding his return; Elon Musk has thrown his support behind the effort, and US President Donald Trump said he would not mind seeing Huang reinstated as CEO. Thousands of Nvidia-identifying supporters joined the call even as governance experts and some investors warn that bringing him back before investigations are complete could expose the company to fresh risks. The groundswell has turned a corporate succession story into a test of whether Nvidia can separate itself from a founder whose influence stretches across its employees, shareholders, Silicon Valley, the Taiwanese supply chain, and Washington. Taiwan's tallest skyscraper, Taipei 101, was illuminated on Monday with messages including 'Taiwan Loves Jensen.' Some prominent shareholders such as Atreides Management's Gavin Baker and Altimeter Capital Management CEO Brad Gerstner have urged Nvidia not to rush to replace him before all the facts were known. The support comes as US intelligence agencies are still trying to determine the extent of Alice Huang's relationship with China's Ministry of State Security and what information she may have passed to Beijing; evidence gathered so far indicates she was likely an intelligence asset rather than a fully trained spy. The uncertainty has divided investors over Huang's future and complicated the board's search for a successor. Nvidia shares fell 3.7% on Monday, a day before the chipmaker is due to report third-quarter earnings. The 'Stand With Jensen' campaign listed SpaceX and Tesla CEO Elon Musk, Replit CEO Amjad Masad, and Epic Games CEO Tim Sweeney among its signatories; more than 8,800 identified themselves as current Nvidia employees and more than 94,000 as shareholders, though the website cautioned that professional affiliations were self-reported and had not been independently verified. Huang stepped down on Thursday after reports of alleged affairs with employees plunged the AI chip heavyweight into crisis. Trump's reported trades this year suggest he held between $13 million and $62 million in Nvidia stock as of the end of August, per a Washington Post review of his financial disclosures. US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent has called for Nvidia to appoint an outsider as its next CEO, saying the company needs a 'dramatic shake-up' following Huang's departure. Independent technology researcher Richard Windsor said he expected large institutional investors to oppose Huang's return while investigations remained unresolved because of legal exposure and uncertainty; yet his own view was that shareholders would ultimately be better served by Huang's return because of relationships built with customers and suppliers, particularly TSMC, which manufactures Nvidia's most advanced chips. Nowhere is Huang's unusual reach more visible than in Taiwan, where he was born before moving to the United States as a child; for many Taiwanese his exit marks the loss of a charismatic champion who helped put the island at the heart of the global AI boom. Jimmy Yang, 42, said Huang's departure was a loss for Taiwan and expressed hope that Huang could eventually return, drawing a parallel with Apple co-founder Steve Jobs, who returned after being forced out.
items.title: Nvidia Board Rules Out Jensen Huang's Return Amid Growing Campaign and China-Link Investigation

items.summary:
A software bug in Microsoft's productivity suite caused a global outage after routine traffic rerouting on Nov. 11 triggered the system to malfunction, exhausting server memory and causing servers critical to Outlook, Teams, Copilot AI assistant and other services to fail for about 15 hours before Microsoft realized the problem at around 11:30 a.m. on Nov. 12.

The bug had been lurking undetected in the company's data centers since July because its testing protocols simulated traffic patterns and hardware that did not reflect real-world conditions, with tests typically focusing on older and weaker systems rather than newer hardware where the bug is more destructive due to greater processing power. As soon as servers returned to service, they were overwhelmed by waiting traffic and failed again.

Charles Lamanna, Microsoft's executive vice president overseeing workplace software, apologized early Monday for the outage in a post on X social media site that offered detail on what went wrong. The company issued a preliminary report to customers late Sunday, then spent another 15 hours identifying and starting to roll out the fix. At the nadir on Thursday, more than 80% of the servers behind Outlook were unresponsive.

The outage was an embarrassment for Microsoft and a reminder of the risks of relying so heavily on a single technology vendor. Shares were down about 1% at 2:29 p.m. on Monday.
items.title: Microsoft 365 Outage: Software Bug Went Unnoticed Since July

items.summary: India's digital payments ecosystem is grappling with a category of fraud that extends beyond user error, prompting calls for deeper intervention at the operating system level. For years, awareness around Unified Payments Interface (UPI) fraud centered on careless mistakes—sharing OTPs, scanning fake QR codes, or approving deceptive 'collect' requests. However, officials now point to vulnerabilities originating in Android itself, which existing security solutions may fail to detect or prevent and which lie beyond the control of individual customer-facing payment apps.
items.title: NPCI and UPI apps turn to Google to address Android security vulnerabilities behind frauds

items.summary:
CNN reported that US intelligence indicates Iran is developing contingency plans to potentially target senior Trump administration officials in Washington, DC with a radioactive dirty bomb or chemical weapons. The reporting quoted seven US officials familiar with the intelligence and pointed to specific potential locations within the capital, prompting American authorities to step up contingency planning. However, officials cautioned that these preparations do not necessarily signal an imminent attack or a decision by Tehran to execute such a plot; one source described them as 'prudent,' while another noted uncertainty over whether Iran has personnel in place to carry out operations. Two officials said several meetings were held over the past week to discuss countermeasures.

The White House stated it was monitoring potential threats but maintained there was no immediate credible threat to the US mainland, with spokesperson Lauren Bis saying 'at this time there are no credible threats to the homeland.' Officials view the intelligence as a possible sign that Tehran is considering escalating conflict beyond the Middle East amid continued American military pressure and an economic blockade. One source noted Iranian communications suggested bomb-making materials may have been stored inside the United States, though officials remain divided over both the credibility of this information and Iran's operational capability.

The reported threat comes against a backdrop of stalled diplomatic efforts to end the conflict between Washington and Tehran, centered on the Strait of Hormuz. US President Donald Trump said last week the war would be 'over fairly soon,' even as tensions persist. American officials believe acquiring radioactive material is one of the main challenges in assembling such a device; a source described any weapon like it as 'a weapon of terror, not a weapon of precision.'

Separate concerns involve chemical attacks on US troops stationed in the Middle East, with several officials raising worries that American forces may lack adequate protective equipment or training. The intelligence also raises questions about detection capabilities amid uncertainty over a key surveillance law allowing collection of communications involving foreign nationals; orders approved before its June expiry remain valid until March 2027.

Attorney General Todd Blanche, Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton and CIA Director John Ratcliffe wrote to Republican and Democratic leaders last week urging reauthorization. In their letter they argued delays would 'put the lives of both Americans in the homeland and our troops stationed abroad at risk,' briefing lawmakers on Iran several days earlier; a US official cautioned that if Iranian leadership views regime survival as at stake, it could take otherwise unacceptable risks.
items.title: US intelligence warns Iran planning possible dirty bomb or chemical attack on Washington officials amid stalled conflict

items.summary: President Trump suggested that Jensen Huang, the ousted ex-CEO of Nvidia, could return to lead the company. He said Huang had 'learned a big lesson' and he 'would certainly not mind' if Huang were reinstated, adding that there was 'a big group of people that would like him to return.' These comments arrived as a 'Stand with Jensen' petition gathered momentum among current and former Nvidia staff, investors, and Silicon Valley supporters including SpaceX's Elon Musk and Epic Games CEO Tim Sweeney. The petition calls on the board to bring back Huang while an independent investigation proceeds or until there is compelling evidence that his departure serves the company's best interests. Even Dan Ives, a Yorkville financial analyst who once called Huang the 'Godfather of AI,' said Huang's return was hopeless; after this global scandal, he wrote, 'the old Jensen with the black leather jacket and rock star persona is gone for good.' Corporate governance expert Charles Elson argued that many in Silicon Valley remain out of touch with American public sentiment given the national security threat, noting that Huang violated the company's own ethics rules. He criticized the 'genius theory' — the belief that whatever a genius does is forgivable and geniuses have their own rules of the road — calling it a terrible way to run both a business and a country. The uncertainty over Nvidia's future sent its stock down 4.1% at Monday's close, dragging the S&P 500 nearly 2%, marking a third straight loss. Huang resigned last week after revelations that he had extramarital affairs — one with Alice Huang, a Chinese businesswoman suspected of being an intelligence asset for Beijing, and another with a senior executive who reported to him. Colette Kress has stepped in as interim CEO while the board searches for a replacement. Trump's endorsement comes a day after Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent called for a 'dramatic shake-up' in Nvidia's leadership on Fox News, saying the next CEO should come from outside the company. Questions about Trump's role are mounting after New York Times reporting that he was told last year and again earlier this year that Huang was having an affair with a woman U.S. intelligence had determined was a Beijing spy — but did nothing about it. On Monday, Trump downplayed the scandal: 'Nobody's proven that she's a spy,' he said, adding that any beautiful Chinese woman labeled a spy is being unfairly targeted. He suggested more investigation was needed. The Financial Times reported Huang has been discussing his possible return with confidants as allies assemble a 'war room' of Silicon Valley supporters. Petition organizers questioned whether Alice Huang — a former executive at Singapore-based Megaspeed — was truly a spy, stating they had not seen evidence substantiating the allegation and were concerned that Jensen was removed without meaningful due process. Jeffrey Sonnenfeld of the Yale School of Management said the apparent national security threat was only one of Huang's possible wrongs, pointing to a long list suggesting he abused his position while the board failed in its oversight duties. He noted that sleeping with a direct report is a fireable offense and raised questions about Huang's judgment, fairness, and compliance with corporate governance norms. Sonnenfeld also flagged that Trump personally holds millions of dollars of Nvidia stock — reported by the Washington Post as possibly having increased to more than $60 million in August — and that an investment bank run by Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick's sons does business financing deals involving Nvidia customers. The identities of petition signatories could not be independently verified, with affiliations described as self-reported. Organizers urged institutional investors backing Huang to dial into the company's next quarterly earnings call scheduled for 5 p.m. Eastern time Tuesday. While some in Silicon Valley took a cautious approach — OpenAI CEO Sam Altman said Jensen has long been 'a hero of mine' but that heroes have flaws and he did not know enough about Nvidia's troubles to say whether Huang should return as CEO, recalling his own removal from the role in 2023 before being reinstated — others remained resolute. The leadership scandal has thrown the wider artificial intelligence industry into turmoil because Nvidia is a key player in the AI boom, with its chips vital for cloud computing and data centers underpinning the technology. Huang was a driving force in building the company into a tech giant since co-founding it more than three decades ago.
items.title: Trump Backs Jensen Huang's Nvidia Return Amid Spy Scandal and Industry Turmoil

items.summary: In an interview with reporters on Monday in New Delhi, IBM chairman and CEO Arvind Krishna said the company is holding talks for at least two large projects in India beyond the Amravati Quantum Tech Park. He declined to name those other two projects until he receives a signature and funding confirmation, but described them as serious undertakings similar in nature to the first. Krishna remained upbeat about IBM's expansion of its footprint in India and increased hiring there. On investment scale, he said IBM spends and invests about $3 billion a year in India — significant compared with most others in quantum — while noting that only a fraction of its global number flows into the country. He referenced an earlier stated intent to invest roughly $10 billion over five years in quantum alone, which he called significantly above peers' efforts. Turning to semiconductors, Krishna noted the industry is worth about a trillion dollars globally and asked how much India produces today; he suggested that figure sits around $3 billion and urged India to reach at least 5% of global output as a benchmark for seriousness. He also advised Indian government to scale existing bets before taking new ones. On AI deployment, Krishna observed that very little is currently done from an Indian base but affirmed India has the ingredients to grow large; he noted AI may displace about 10-20% of jobs, with higher risk in sectors such as BPO, while roles evolve — programmers becoming system engineers rather than writing code. He pointed out that roughly half the code IBM writes today is already produced by AI, and that employment continues to rise across locations, having doubled entry-level hiring going into 2026 from 2025.
items.title: IBM CEO Arvind Krishna Signals Two New Large India Projects and Rising Quantum Investment

items.summary:
The US Department of Commerce introduced new export controls on advanced semiconductors and overseas data centres, seeking to prevent companies linked to countries of concern from accessing significant computing power based on US technology. The measures are designed to close potential loopholes through which restricted entities could use advanced US-made chips via foreign infrastructure without directly importing them. Under an interim final rule (IFR), the restrictions target overseas data centres that remotely provide substantial computing capacity to companies headquartered in countries classified under Country Group D:5 or Macau, aiming to prevent such jurisdictions from using advanced semiconductors to train sophisticated AI models.

The new regulations also add licensing requirements for some advanced semiconductor exports and transfers. These apply specifically to five countries — Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and Brazil — which Washington considers to present a higher-than-normal risk of diversion. An exemption remains available for shipments destined for companies headquartered in the US or whose ultimate parent companies are based there, provided they meet specified reporting requirements.

The rules require data centres, foreign chip fabrication facilities and chip exporters to conduct robust due diligence on customers, examining whether those entities are directly or indirectly owned or controlled by individuals or organizations in restricted jurisdictions. The licensing requirement does not cover commercial recommendation systems used by online retailers and social media platforms, which the Commerce Department said do not pose the same national security risks.

The interim rule also formally rescinds the regulations implementing the Biden administration's AI Diffusion Rule, a framework that had never been enforced. This shift signals Washington moving toward greater emphasis on identifying diversion routes, scrutinizing ownership structures and monitoring access to computing infrastructure.

These developments come amid growing scrutiny of Nvidia and its CEO Jensen Huang following allegations that advanced AI servers powered by the company's chips were smuggled into China in violation of American export controls. In March, US authorities charged Super Micro Computer founder and two others with allegedly smuggling servers containing Nvidia-powered hardware worth $2.5 billion to China through intermediaries.

While the latest regulations do not specifically target Nvidia or directly reference the Megaspeed investigation, they address a broader vulnerability in the global AI semiconductor supply chain: access to advanced computing power through overseas infrastructure. The central question is no longer just whether restricted countries can import advanced chips, but whether they can access the computing power those chips deliver through facilities located elsewhere.
items.title: US Tightens AI Chip Export Rules Amid Nvidia Smuggling Controversy

items.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi arrived in Manila for the India-ASEAN and East Asia Summit meetings, stating that his visit would inject new energy into India's partnership with Southeast Asian nations and reinforce collective commitment to a peaceful, prosperous and resilient Indo-Pacific. Soon after landing, he attended a dinner hosted by Philippines President Ferdinand Marcos Jr ahead of Tuesday's multilateral and bilateral engagements. Although no bilateral meeting with US President Trump had been scheduled as late as Monday evening, official sources confirmed the Quad leaders' summit would proceed that night; Modi was expected to return to India late on Tuesday. On Tuesday morning he attended a groundbreaking ceremony at a gurudwara before participating in the 23rd ASEAN-India Summit. In his departure statement from Delhi, Modi emphasized that India's relationship with ASEAN countries is central to its Act East Policy and occupies a key place within its MAHASAGAR vision, describing ties rooted in centuries of civilisational exchange as having grown into a dynamic partnership spanning trade, connectivity, maritime security, technology and people-to-people relations. He also expressed anticipation for building on the Comprehensive Strategic Partnership at the ASEAN-India Summit to advance shared aspirations for growth, connectivity and prosperity, while noting he would interact with the Indian community in the Philippines. Modi further highlighted the East Asia Summit as an important platform for dialogue on regional and global challenges. The Quad leaders' summit—described as the first such meeting since Trump returned to the White House—is expected to draw maximum attention in India and possibly Japan; amid speculation that Trump might have downgraded the Quad, it is anticipated to reaffirm commitment rather than announce fresh initiatives across shared interests including maritime security, critical technologies, supply chains, connectivity, health and economic security. The US framed its 'partnership of action' around peace, prosperity and security in the Indo-Pacific region. As Trump heads into a trilateral summit with Chinese counterpart Xi Jinping and Russian counterpart Vladimir Putin in Shenzhen, observers will watch whether he tones down Quad rhetoric on China or modulates messaging regarding the South and East China Seas.
items.title: Modi's Manila Visit: Asean Ties Central to India's Act East Policy Amid Quad Summit and Trump-APEC Travel

items.summary: Self-enumeration for the population enumeration phase of Census 2027 began on Monday across Uttar Pradesh, Punjab, Goa and non-snow-bound areas of Uttarakhand. The exercise is scheduled to run until November 30, after which house-to-house enumeration will commence from December 1. It will collect data across 40 fields, including caste, with an open-ended question whose reply is recorded as declared by the respondent; no documentary proof or verification is required. Meanwhile, in Manipur the exercise has been postponed until further notice amid demands for an NRC first.
items.title: Census Phase-II Begins in Four States; Postponed in Manipur Amid NRC Demands

items.summary: The NSE-listed stock closed at a record high of ₹2,070.05 on the BSE, up 4.02% from its previous close (s0). Its market value stood at ₹5.12 lakh crore, making it India's 10th most valued listed company and taking it past Life Insurance Corporation of India (LIC), valued at ₹5.06 lakh crore (s1). Reliance Industries remains India's most valued company with a market capitalisation of ₹18.16 lakh crore, followed by Bharti Airtel and Jio Platforms at ₹13.43 lakh crore and ₹12.91 lakh crore, respectively (s2). HDFC Bank, ICICI Bank, SBI, Tata Consultancy Services, Bajaj Finance and L&T are among the other companies in the country's top 10 by market value (s3). NSE shares, which were listed on the BSE on September 24, have gained in nine of the 11 trading sessions so far in November, rising 16.3%, compared with an 8.5% gain in the benchmark Sensex during the month (s5). The stock has gained around 16% against the company's IPO price of ₹1,785 per share (s6).
items.title: NSE Joins Rs 5 Lakh Crore Market-Cap Club and Overtakes LIC in Valuation

items.summary: Urban Company has unveiled a qualified institutional placement (QIP) plan approved by its shareholders on Sunday, aiming to raise Rs 2,500 crore. The company intends to allocate Rs 600 crore toward its InstaHelp business, which operates in the high-cash-burn instant househelp space, with around Rs 540 crore earmarked for marketing initiatives and Rs 200 crore directed at technology development and cloud infrastructure. This fundraise comes as Urban Company engages in a three-way battle in the instant househelp segment against Lightspeed-backed Snabbit and General Catalyst-backed Pronto. The company went public in September of last year, raising Rs 472 crore through a fresh issue of shares. As of September 30, it held Rs 1,901 crore in cash on its books, while businesses excluding InstaHelp generated Rs 119 crore in adjusted Ebitda over the preceding nine months. During the company's October 16 earnings call, cofounder and CEO Abhiraj Singh Bhal noted that reported losses reflected a deliberate investment strategy rather than competitive pressure, with spending plans mapped out for the next six to eight quarters.
items.title: Urban Company Unveils Rs 2,500 Crore QIP to Fund InstaHelp and Growth Initiatives

items.summary: The India Meteorological Department (IMD) has issued a yellow alert for the coasts of Andhra Pradesh and adjoining South Odisha as Cyclone Akvan, currently a deep depression in the Bay of Bengal, intensifies into a cyclonic storm. The system moved at 10 kmph over the past six hours until 5.30 pm, centered approximately 790 km south of Gopalpur in Odisha. IMD Director General Mrutunjay Mohapatra noted that Odisha is likely to experience heavy rainfall but not extremely heavy rainfall as seen during Cyclone Arnab, which made landfall in Andhra Pradesh on October 28. Bhubaneswar Meteorological Centre Director Manorama Mohanty added that the impact of Akvan is expected to be less severe than Arnab's and confirmed no red warning for extremely heavy rainfall has been issued this time. The Met office had previously issued orange warnings (rainfall between 12 cm and 20 cm) and yellow warnings (rainfall between 7 cm and 11 cm) across various districts in Odisha from November 18 to 21. Akvan is very likely to intensify into a very severe cyclonic storm around November 19 morning, with maximum sustained winds of 120-130 kmph gusting to 145 kmph as it crosses Andhra Pradesh between Nellore and Tuni around noon the following day. This marks the third cyclonic storm formed over the Bay of Bengal in three weeks.
items.title: IMD Issues Yellow Alert as Cyclone Akvan Intensifies Ahead of Landfall in Andhra Pradesh and Odisha
